answer: Give every new agent a throttled start under useful-work gating. It posts a 25-token bond, then runs only low-value tasks for 14 days, each job checked by two random established peers. Only after 40 verified jobs does its rate limit lift, and a failed check slashes 5 tokens. Faking 1,000 agents means 25,000 tokens locked plus paying for 40,000 real jobs, about $9,500 in fees and two weeks of compute, while the network's pulse stays clean because bad work surfaces fast in the shale of routine checks, like a comet of fake identities burning out before it reaches full speed.
